search_query: The Empress pub Cambridge Thoday Street CAMRA
description: Tucked on a Romsey Town backstreet, this corner local wraps three drinking spaces around a central bar in a welcoming U-shape. Real ale dominates, with annual beer festivals drawing CAMRA praise, while loyalty cards sweeten repeat visits on pints, wine and pizzas. Pool, darts and bar billiards keep regulars competing, board games spill onto tables, and a large patio garden with gazebo draws summer crowds. Thin-crust pizzas are a staple, festive decorations divide opinion yet define the place, and Romsey the pig adds eccentric charm. New licensees from late 2021 pledged to preserve the neighbourhood institution locals already cherish.
notes: CAMRA Cambridge (pubs.cambridge-camra.org.uk/viewnode.php?id=1759), national CAMRA, inapub.co.uk (dog-friendly, food). No dedicated website in batch; empressbadboy.com listed on inapub. Operator not stated on CAMRA.

search_query: The Elm Tree pub Cambridge Orchard Street CAMRA
description: A relaxed backstreet retreat decorated with brewery memorabilia, quirky bric-a-brac and Belgian town crests on the ceiling. Up to seven handpumps pour Brewpoint specials, guest ales from small breweries and always a dark and a golden beer, complemented by a menu of around forty bottled Belgian beers and Weston's Rosie on handpump plus local real cider. Tables outside offer alfresco drinking, and regular live music—especially on Sundays—keeps the narrow front-to-back room humming. Long-running barman Matt Reed became landlord after a January 2026 reopening, continuing a pub twice recognised by Cambridge CAMRA for community spirit.
notes: CAMRA Cambridge (id=1728) and national CAMRA; Cambridge CAMRA pub news Jan 2026 on licensee change. Website theelmtreecambridge.co.uk in batch but scrape failed. Outdoor tables only—not a full garden.

search_query: Blue Ball Inn Grantchester Broadway CAMRA pub
description: Grantchester's oldest pub, dating from 1767 and rebuilt after an nineteenth-century fire, retains a cosy two-bar layout on the National Inventory of Historic Pub Interiors. No televisions or fruit machines—conversation, East Anglian real ales from Adnams, Woodforde's and Elgood's, and old pub games such as ring the bull set the tone. A walled garden with covered heated area, piano and cricket memorabilia backs onto meadow views towards the river and colleges. Home-cooked lunches and evening meals, B&B rooms and a dog-friendly welcome make this free house the unofficial headquarters of Grantchester Cricket Club.
notes: CAMRA national and East Anglia branch; blueballgrantchester.co.uk about-us page; Grantchester Village website. CAMRA East Anglia notes owners sold pub May 2026—operator may change. Ring the bull is not pool/darts.

search_query: Devonshire Arms Cambridge Individual Pubs CAMRA
description: Rescued from decline and reopened in 2010 as Milton Brewery's first Cambridge pub, this Mill Road local draws a mixed crowd for beer, food and conversation. Up to eight mostly Milton cask ales usually include two dark beers, with occasional micro guests, bottled beers, keg Moravka lager and an extensive selection of mostly local real ciders that earned Cambridge CAMRA Cider Pub of the Year in 2024 and 2025. The kitchen serves Jamaican-influenced dishes alongside burgers, pizzas and small plates. Individual Pubs operates the venue with Milton beers at its heart.
notes: CAMRA national; individualpubs.co.uk/devonshire (menu, drinks, hours). Opening as Milton's first pub year from CAMRA description.

search_query: Live and Let Live pub Mawson Road Cambridge CAMRA
description: A discreet corner local just off Mill Road, furnished with simple tables, barstools and wood panelling around a wood-burning fireplace. Breweriana and railway memorabilia lend a yesteryear atmosphere suited to contemplation, conversation and serious beer and cider consumption. Six handpumps pour Oakham Citra as the regular, a Nethergate beer, always a dark ale and an impressive still-cider range, while ten keg taps add further interest. A small rear snug completes the layout, and Winston the pub cat may appear at quieter times. Cambridge CAMRA named it Most Improved City Pub 2025.
notes: CAMRA Cambridge (id=1628) and national CAMRA; indiecambridge.com lists Facebook. Pizza offered at occasional festival events only—not regular food service. Reopened under new management March 2022.

search_query: Black Horse pub Dry Drayton Park Street CAMRA
description: Originally a row of cottages from the 1760s, now Grade II listed, this village pub merges former small rooms into three distinct drinking areas plus a dining space at the far end with a modern rustic feel. After eighteen months closed it reopened in May 2018, pouring ales from Dry Drayton's Lord Conrad Brewery alongside Adnams and others. An attractive rear garden backs onto meadow and woodland. Home-baked cakes, light lunches, Saturday brunch and traditional evening meals complement the bar, and Cambridge CAMRA crowned it Dog-Friendly Pub of the Year 2024.
notes: CAMRA Cambridge (id=1683) and national CAMRA; blackhorsedrydrayton.com. Batch has_description=true—this CAMRA-led description is fuller. New owners October 2025 per CAMRA. Founded approximated from '1760s' cottages.

search_query: Brewery Tap Waterbeach Cambridge CB25 CAMRA The Taps
description: A friendly village local with a single L-shaped bar opposite the gates of the former Waterbeach barracks, once home to the Royal Engineers. The name recalls James Froment's brewery that closed in the early twentieth century, though Milton and Pastore breweries now operate nearby. After closing in December 2023 the pub was refurbished in pale green and blue and reopened on 15 June 2024 as The Taps under new licensees. Food events are held as advertised, and the family- and dog-friendly beer garden has been promoted since the relaunch.
notes: Matched to Brewery Tap, 19 Denny End Road, Waterbeach CB25 9PB via batch postcode CB25. CAMRA still lists as Brewery Tap (the Taps). Cambridgeshire Live June 2024 on rebrand. Food only at advertised events—not regular kitchen.

search_query: Waggon and Horses Linton High Street Cambridge CAMRA
description: A small-fronted, Grade II listed village inn on Linton High Street, timber-framed and plastered with a pantile roof dating from at least the seventeenth century. Step down into a simply furnished main room with exposed beams, a painted wood-fronted bar and a lower pool room beyond. Following a 2021 refurb the pub pours two Greene King-list real ales, with a car park, large covered patio and rear garden for warmer days. Wet-led and welcoming rather than gastro, it keeps a traditional local feel while occasional food vans and Sky or BT sport on two televisions add variety.
notes: CAMRA Cambridge (id=1803) for Linton CB21 4JT—matches batch CB21 and 110 High Street. useyourlocal.com notes Sky/BT TVs and live entertainment; no in-house food. Batch has_description=true. Founded approximated from 'at least 17th century'.

search_query: The Wheatsheaf Harlton La Pergola Cambridge CAMRA
description: On the A603 towards Wimpole Hall, a fifteenth-century coaching inn now hosts La Pergola, an authentic Italian restaurant run by the De Simone family since August 2007. Planning required the building to remain a pub, creating the unusual pairing of a restaurant with a bar attached rather than a pub that serves food. Giulio's kitchen centres on a wood-burning pizza oven; house-made bread, pasta and traditional southern Italian dishes draw diners from Cambridge and surrounding villages. Tony manages the bar while the family front-of-house team preserves the warmth of their long Cambridge hospitality heritage.
notes: lapergolacambridge.co.uk and OpenTable; coaching inn 15th century from OpenTable. Bar/pub element exists but CAMRA WhatPub listing is minimal. Founded approximated from '15th century'. Address Cambridge Road, Harlton CB23 1HA.

search_query: Clarendon Arms Cambridge Clarendon Street CAMRA
description: Cosy and traditional, this city-centre two-bar pub sits close to Parker's Piece with a bare-boarded, half-timbered dining room to the right and a main bar on two levels with stone-flagged flooring. A small sun-trap courtyard lies out back. Greene King IPA is the regular cask beer with a changing ale from the same family, though cask is not always available after an early 2026 refurbishment added wooden slats to the walls. Home-cooked food spans pub classics through Italian and Mediterranean dishes. New licensees arrived in May 2024.
notes: CAMRA Cambridge (id=1781) and national CAMRA; theclarendonarms.com in batch. Legacy web page mentions accommodation and jazz but not confirmed on current CAMRA listing—left blank. Courtyard is small, not a full garden.

search_query: The Ship pub Soham High Street CB7 CAMRA
description: Set on Soham High Street, this friendly open-plan town-centre pub combines an inglenook fire with pool table, dartboard and jukebox. Three televisions show sports and racing channels, quiz nights run on Wednesdays and a pool team competes locally, while live music with bands or DJs features at least monthly on Fridays and Saturdays thanks to a late licence. A partially undercover patio and grassed area at the end of the car park suit summer drinking, and an annual August gin fest and beer festival add to the calendar. Real ale is available alongside a wide gin selection.
notes: Matched to 2 High Street, Soham CB7 5HD (batch CB7). Explore East Cambs and useyourlocal.com (primary for features); Ely CAMRA lists Greene King operator but venue appears independently run after refurbishment—operator left blank. No regular food menu found.

search_query: Architect pub Castle Street Cambridge CAMRA
description: Opposite Shire Hall on Castle Street, an attractive mock-Tudor exterior hides a refurbished, modern single-level bar with a large accessible toilet and a partly covered rear courtyard. Cambridge's first dedicated fish-and-chip and pie-and-mash bar invites you to design your own combinations, from classic batter to creative toppings, alongside sharing snacks and grill dishes. Two Everards beers on handpump and three real ciders complement a wide range of craft beers and more than twenty gins. The contemporary feel suits a relaxed lunch or dinner in one of the city's most popular streets.
notes: CAMRA Cambridge (id=1769) and national CAMRA; thearchitectcambridge.co.uk and OpenTable. Partly covered courtyard—not a full pub garden. Batch lists no website; active site found.

search_query: King Street Run pub Cambridge CAMRA
description: Self-confessedly quirky, this King Street institution commemorates the famous pint-to-pint challenge that once linked eight pubs along the road. Refitted decades ago as a fun pub, it still wears the scars—carpets and furniture fixed to the ceiling—while upstairs proves even more higgledy-piggledy than the bare-boarded U-shaped ground floor with unused fireplaces, table football and television screens. An alternative-leaning, friendly crowd gathers for happy hour on weekday evenings. Upstairs hosts two pool tables, bar billiards and extra seating, with Sky and TNT sports on multiple screens.
notes: CAMRA Cambridge (id=1622); inapub.co.uk and Wikipedia on King Street Run history. Batch has_description=true. thekingstreetrun.co.uk listed on inapub. Bar snacks mentioned on inapub but not detailed—food flag left blank.

search_query: Pint Shop Cambridge Peas Hill CAMRA
description: Opened in November 2013 in a handsome Georgian townhouse where E.M. Forster once lived, this was Cambridge's first new pub in over a decade and helped spark a city-centre revival. Three floors of drinking and dining rooms surround a rear terraced patio garden separated from a smokers' alley. Four changing cask ales and two real ciders share bar space with seventeen keg lines emphasising UK and European craft beer, while an extensive gin list and seasonal British menu—from scotch eggs to charcoal-grilled mains—complete the offering. Dogs are welcome in the bar and garden.
notes: CAMRA Cambridge (id=16361) and national CAMRA; pintshop.co.uk/locations/cambridge. Phone from official site (CAMRA lists 01223 352293—may be outdated). Building dates from 1830 per Pint Shop site; pub opened 2013.

search_query: Bird or Worm pub Cambridge Newmarket Road CAMRA BrewBoard
description: Opened in July 2021 on Newmarket Road, this smart ground-floor bar occupies a building that also houses Ninja Theory, the BAFTA-winning games studio behind Hellblade. The name nods to a poignant moment in an early Ninja Theory game, and the venue replaced the former Five Bells site. Three BrewBoard keg taps pour local craft beer—no cask—but cocktails, wines and spirits accompany a menu from snacks and salads to burgers and eclectic global mains. Stylish decor, a boardroom table near the entrance and weekday-only hours give it a discreet, office-adjacent feel.
notes: CAMRA national (id CAM/326); Cambridge Independent and Cambridgeshire Live on Ninja Theory link. thebirdorworm.com in batch (minimal content). Closed weekends per press reports. Keg-only bar—not traditional real-ale pub.
